key_insight: Learning-curve shape depends primarily on how situations occur: uniform occurrence yields exponential learning, while power-law occurrence yields power-law learning.
engineering_relevance: The framework connects learning laws across natural and artificial systems and addresses choosing a training distribution that differs from deployment.
method: Define learning level as the probability that the next situation has been mastered and not forgotten.
Derive learning curves from situation-occurrence distributions.
Relate power-law and exponential mechanisms to neural scaling laws and constant-contraction processes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical derivations and cross-domain theoretical connections, but no empirical datasets, benchmarks, or quantitative validation.
watch_item: Different mechanisms can produce indistinguishable learning curves, so curve shape alone cannot identify a system’s internal learning structure.
paper_title: Learning curves in natural and artificial systems
